Hey [~accountid:5b7bea09d08e47445d6fd01e] 

It will be difficult to separate impact of just this thing. Driver fraud is not easily measurable on its own. What we can check is the overall market fraud if it grows upwards. But also you need to consider that the fraud is a live thing, consisted of many different aspects and patterns, but also multiple different rules and solution that we apply, all in the same time. 
Another thing to consider is that most of the driver fraud will be failed payment, so even the last 2,3 weeks will be early to tell, because we always expect recovery in the upcoming month for part of those failed payments, so we can check this again after some time for recovery has been allowed. 
But in general, what we saw with other markets as well, it is expected that the fraud would increase when the fraud engine has been turned off for the driver fraud. 
Here is a 1 month (weekly split) actual numbers for PT at the moment. And we have a week-over-week predicted fraud state for the past 2 weeks of 0.26% to 0.30%

Hi there!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are complying, therefore, we are allowing them to financially gain.

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action the user.

On a different note, kindly be more precise in your escalations in the future and give as many details as possible about your case in order for our team to assist you best. Just links and a few words won’t do. Some examples to consider or think about: _What makes this case significant? How did you discover the matter? What is the current situation? What is suspicious in your opinion exactly? What have you already done? Who have you consulted on the matter?_ *_What is the expected outcome? What would you like us or propose to do?_* _What is the impact of this issue on GMV and count? What is the urgency of the issue?_

Cheers,

Batteries are included in the hazardous waste category. 

Used oils are collected separately, in hermetically sealed containers, resistant to mechanical and thermal shock. The used oils presenting different characteristics are not mixed with each other or with other types of waste or substances, they are stored in suitable containers in appropriately arranged, fenced and secured spaces, to prevent uncontrolled leaks. Producers and holders of used oils are obliged to hand over the entire amount free of charge only to economic operators authorised to carry out collection activities.

Metal is collected separately, like other waste (glass, cardboard, plastic).

Tire manufacturers/importers, economic agents that sell new tires and/or used tires have the obligation to report their quantitative records to the Environmental Protection Agency.

# *partnerDriver/startAuthentication* for phone login

BE returns the nonce value when driver tries to log in and upon receiving a nonce value, *startAuthentication* endpoint is called to verify user for appstore verification
In cases when appstore verif is turned on, verification fails with a generic message _“something went wrong, try again later on the UI”_ 
When *getAuthenticationConfiguration* endpoint returns an error, we retry endpoint.
When g*etAuthenticationConfiguration* returns an empty string or null, we consider this as verification being turned off.

If you do not consent to your image and identity documents being automatically checked and would prefer to have your identity verified manually by a member of our verification team, please tap [_*_here]_*_. Additionally we would also ask to use the same font sizes and colorings throughout the text, so it would not seem as if we are nudging the user to make a certain decision. 

We also need to ensure we record the date/time stamp of the consent in our back-end systems (i.e. when the driver clicks apply and uses the automated verification process). Which is campaign_total_spending

Current explore is:
[https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/rides/campaigns_total_spending?qid=3lfBeS68QVIs6zlP4h0pmP|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/rides/campaigns_total_spending?qid=3lfBeS68QVIs6zlP4h0pmP]



Here’s how discounts are calculated on SQL level:

[https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/projects/kpi/files/presto_views/campaigns_total_spending.view.lkml?line=13|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/projects/kpi/files/presto_views/campaigns_total_spending.view.lkml?line=13]

**

{noformat}    SELECT
            o.city_id,
            o.country,
            ot.price_currency AS currency,
            f.company_type as vehicle_type,
            COALESCE(AVG(rates.rate), 1) AS conversion_rate,
            COALESCE(SUM(ot.price), 0) AS total_client_price,
            COALESCE(SUM(ot.ride_price), 0) AS total_ride_price,
            COALESCE(SUM(ot.ride_price - ot.price), 0) AS all_rider_bonus_costs,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN invite_usg.order_try_id IS NOT NULL or invite_usg_new.order_try_id IS NOT NULL THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS invite_receiver_bonus_costs,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN invite_bns_usg.order_try_id IS NOT NULL or invite_bns_usg_new.order_try_id IS NOT NULL THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS invite_sender_bonus_costs,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN target_camp.use_rules LIKE '%is_first_ride%' THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS targeted_campaign_costs_first_ride,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN target_camp.id IS NOT NULL THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS targeted_campaign_costs_not_first_ride,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN target_camp.name LIKE '%sign%' AND target_camp.use_rules LIKE '%is_first_ride%' THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS signup_costs_first_ride,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN ((target_camp.spend_objective = 'activation') and (target_camp.name  not like '%09_4M_NA%') and (target_camp.name not like '%not_activated%') and (target_camp.name not like '%NANH%') and (target_camp.name not like '%LPT_NA%')) THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS signup_costs,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN (target_camp.id IS NOT NULL) and (target_camp.spend_target_absolute > 0) and (target_camp.spend_target_gmv_percentage > 0) and (target_camp.bonus_type = 'percentage_of_ride_price') THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS targeted_campaign_costs_dcc,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN event_camp.use_rules LIKE '%is_first_ride%' THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS event_campaign_costs_first_ride,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN event_camp.id IS NOT NULL THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS event_campaign_costs_not_first_ride,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN dd_usg.order_try_id IS NOT NULL THEN ot.ride_price - ot.price END), 0) AS dynamic_discount_bonus_costs,
            DATE(DATE_ADD('hour', timezone_hour(at_timezone(o.created, timezone)), o.created)) AS period
      FROM ng_public.company_order o
      JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON ot.order_id=o.id AND ot.city_id=o.city_id AND ot.state = 'finished'
      JOIN ng_public.fleet_company f ON f.id= ot.driver_company_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_user_invite_code_usage invite_usg ON invite_usg.order_try_id = ot.id AND invite_usg.used_by_user_id = o.user_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_user_invite_bonus_code_usage invite_bns_usg ON invite_bns_usg.order_try_id = ot.id
      --joining new tables for the referral campaigns
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_referral_shared_code_usage invite_usg_new ON invite_usg_new.order_try_id = ot.id AND invite_usg_new.city_id = ot.city_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_referral_earned_code_usage invite_bns_usg_new ON invite_bns_usg_new.order_try_id = ot.id AND invite_bns_usg_new.city_id = ot.city_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_targeted_campaign_code_usage targeted_usg ON targeted_usg.order_try_id = ot.id AND targeted_usg.user_id = o.user_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_event_campaign_code_usage event_usg ON event_usg.order_try_id = ot.id AND event_usg.user_id = o.user_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_targeted_campaign target_camp ON target_camp.id = targeted_usg.targeted_campaign_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_event_campaign event_camp ON event_camp.id = event_usg.event_campaign_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_dynamic_campaign_code_usage dd_usg ON dd_usg.order_try_id = ot.id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.campaign_dynamic_campaign dd_camp ON dd_camp.id = dd_usg.campaign_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates rates ON ot.price_currency = rates.currency and DATE(o.created)=DATE(rates.valid_on)
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city city ON city.id=o.city_id
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,19{noformat}

Found and reproduced the most possible scenario.

* On systemd service stopping system waits for 18 sec and kills {{docker --attach}} with SIGKILL because docker stop has lower timeout (18 sec). It causes leaking of FD opened by {{docker --attach}}.
* Subsequent restart by node-monitor would worsen the situation because executing {{docker --attach <HANG CONTAINER ID>}} leads to new leaked FDs.

service:

{noformat}ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker stop -t 22 $SERVICE_NAME
TimeoutStopSec=18{noformat}

The easy fix would be increasing systemd timeout to let Docker to terminate the container and gracefully close the socket.

Hey! Instructions to add to the article:
- Provide initial context for CS: The companies usually with invoice billing as payment method will send the proof of payment once they have done the bank transfer for their outstanding debt.
- The payment only needs to be manually matched by Commerce if they don’t add the Reference number to the bank transfer. The reference number is always the same, and is usually sent to the company in the outstanding amount reminder e-mail, but can also be consulted by the company in the Business Portal > Billing. On our end, we can check the reference number for each company on their admin page (v1), under “businessBankRequisites”.
- Before going to the Payment data page, the agent should check the company’s page on Admin, on the Payments tab, to see if the amount was already reflected in their account.
- When searching on the “Payment data” page, I wouldn’t recommend only searching for “rejected” payments, as the payment can also be showing in the “pending” state.
- When you locate the specific payment page, check the “Details” to check both the Company’s name and the Reference Number. If the reference number is there and the payment status is “pending” this means that it won’t be necessary to escalate the case to Commerce. The amount will be reflected soon.

!Screenshot 2023-04-24 at 15.04.30.png|width=586,height=357!

- If the reference number is not there, it will be necessary to raise a ticket to Commerce.
- After creating the SD ticket, inform the business admin that the document will be analyzed and that we will provide them with a confirmation as soon as possible. Extremely important to mention that, if they wish for this procedure to be even more agile in the future, they should add the reference number to the bank transfer (and indicate their designated reference number). Leave the ticket on-hold until you receive a response from Commerce. 

Please let me know if you need any further clarification from my end. It’s extremely important for us to be as thorough as possible, as Payment Matching is a new subject to most of the agents. Thank you!

Hi Sandro,

Thanks for reaching out. I quickly looked into our numbers in Georgia for Early Cash-outs from the fraud side.

The currently determined minimum number of orders for a driver is 25. The average daily orders for a driver in Georgia are around 9, meaning a driver can request their first Early Cash-out in 3 days or earlier. After the first Early Cash-out, there is no restriction from our side regarding the number of trips, meaning that if drivers had only one order during the day, they still could request the Early Cash-out. So, I see no significant value added if we reduce the number of minimum required orders.

Regarding generally softening the rules: For the last few weeks, we have noticed an increasing trend in failed amounts from the drivers doing Early Cash-out (please see attached).

!GE_FailedPayments_InstantPayout.png|width=91.66666666666667%!

This makes me hesitant to soften the rules for Georgia. I have even been considering reviewing rules for Georgia and tightening them if there is some fraud going on from the drivers’ side. Besides, the number of Early Cash-outs rejected by fraud in the last 3 months is only 144 out of 129666 instant payouts requested.

!Screenshot 2023-04-24 at 12.44.19.png|width=292,height=160!

So, considering all the above, it would be helpful to provide a more detailed explanation (preferably a business case with numbers and examples) of reconsidering the rules from the fraud side.

Best,

Leyla

For testing used a camera stand with a phone attached to it and ruler. For each test made following measurements: 

* Scooter geographical position, taken from [http://xgis.maaamet.ee|http://xgis.maaamet.ee|smart-link] 
* Scooter GPS location - both Phone GPS and Scooter GPS are used. In case of phone, position was taken from a Scooter handlebar
* Scooter VPS location and accuracy - taken from a Scooter handlebar
* 6+ calculated measurements of scooter location. Taken from 1.5m, 2m and 2.5m distance from the scooter

To be investigated/remarks: 

* did not work on Samsung S22+ with Android 13, the tap on screen did not work, but possibly fixable as could be a bug
* startup time - there are two steps: 
** initialization of VPS, here it tries to connect to google cloud, sometimes takes up to 20 seconds and should be optimized
** localization of the position, can take up to 10 seconds and is working faster if move the camera around, this point should be respected and notify user
* accuracy and positioning correlation - the better accuracy the better final position, accuracy is being improved while moving the camera around to take more spots, I’d propose to disable submit button until accuracy is less than 1-1.5m, also considering timeout if during that time accuracy didn’t improve
* detecting scooter boundaries on a photo - ML should be used to detect. Boundaries are needed for formula that calculated distance from camera to the scooter
* camera angle and distance correlation - distance calculation works the best if phone is located on same height as the scooter and in vertical position. I also implemented simple coefficient that takes into consideration phone tilted angle, but it works correct only if the scooter is on the photo center. In case of longer distance, for example 2.5 meters it is possible to take a photo where scooter is on the upper side of photo and in this case phone tilt angle is too big and distance is calculated incorrectly. Have to find better formula or respect the scooter position on the photo

I checked the examples quickly in the ticket and i have some pointers. Most of these scenarios are very very low distances for the driver to reach the rider and this is the majority of the rides in Estonia. If you look at the example some of the locations do not allow even the car to reach exactly the rider or there are even destination changes the rider requested in some orders which increase the price and rides has been compensated for that. 
I think this will be more easily solvable with some communication and education to both riders and drivers. 
On another point, i would also argue that this should be pushed to product side, because as the definition say for the paid wait time fee, driver needs to be at location and wait to start receiving it, so he should not be moving at all, hence all movement and all distance away from the pickup should not even start calculating the wait fee. 
I would run deeper analysis on the top abusers and find a threshold we from fraud side can safely introduce to limit these occurrences. Our solution recalculates the price back and removes the wait fee so driver loses incentive to abuse it. But most of the scenarios will still be left out of that rule, because as i mentioned these are very tricky situations to flag them as fraud and distances are very low and we might end up hurting the supply more rather then solving the issue. 
I will come back with more info after the analysis, on whether it makes sense to make a rule from fraud side.

Hey [~accountid:5cfe57d9a7095c0c3ffac38d] ! 👋 I need help determining how to proceed with the required CS content changes. I’ll share some context and my question.

*Issue reported by the Fraud team*

* The Fraud team discovered a driver fraud scenario when the driver takes a very long route or goes to a very far destination but hasn’t logged the trip destination changes in the app.
* Such drivers report that the customer paid less. They may have submitted a price review or simply reached out to CS reporting that customers paid less than they should have.
* In the UK alone, CS doesn’t recognise these cases as driver fraud and adjusts the price, causing us significant losses (the rider payment fails and we have to compensate drivers).
* The UK CS team has been informed ([thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CM30FTRHP/p1681130605527859] on #uk_updates) about recognising these cases; however, CS still make mistakes. No CS process updates has been made yet.
* The Fraud team wants to enforce this as a global procedure (to prevent this case of driver fraud).

*Changes to make in the related CS processes*
🚗 [Driver reporting undercharged or offline ride|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360010166173--Driver-reporting-undercharged-or-offline-ride]
🚗 [Completing a Price Review|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013391799--Completing-a-Price-Review]

* Ensure that agents recognise these driver fraud cases based on the following criteria:
** Estimated trip distance and duration is very short
** Actual trip distance driven and duration are significantly longer
** Driver didn’t adjust the trip destination in the app
* If such a case is discovered:
** Don’t adjust the final order price
** Educate D to always adjust the trip destination in the app
** No compensations should be provided here

*My question*

Should I:

* just go with incorporating the changes required by the Fraud team (ignoring other process logic issues in these two KB articles), or
* revamp both articles fully? 

I think it’s best to go with option 1, as I fear it may take some time to fully understand price reviews, how they work, and what markets where PRs are disabled do exactly. I fear that Bolt may suffer even more losses until this driver fraud case is covered in the KB and CS are fully capable of recognising these cases. I could review everything related to price reviews holistically and properly at a later sprint to not delay a solution for a pressing issue now. What do you think?

Here, Quentin essentially suggests two changes:

* escalation change (about dirty vehicles)
* change in the logic of the consequences for users leaving the cars dirty

*Escalation change*

* Essentially, it makes sense that if the car is dirty and we have to clean it, it’s better for CS to create a maintenance task as Quentin suggests than to escalate the case via Slack.
* However, the point of the current escalation is not just to notify that the car is dirty - but to prompt the local OPS team to consider charging the user a fine for leaving the car dirty. 
* I’m not sure about the following:
** How often have local OPS in each market actually issued fines based on these specific escalations?
** Should CS escalate all cases (even if there’s no past comments on the user’s profile), or is it best to escalate about serious, repeat offenders? (I believe it’s probably the latter)
* Based on the above, I think it makes sense to add a step (before the escalation) for creating the maintenance task and to evaluate when exactly should CS escalate such cases to local OPS.

*Change in the logic of consequences*

* The logic of consequences for users leaving the cars dirty (0-3 comments and minor/major cases) was introduced as a method to track users that frequently leave cars dirty.
* This is a very primitive and manual way to track this though. I’ve had discussions with the OPS folks and the Car-sharing Product team to create a Car-sharing user behaviour tracking system similar to Driver BQS for Ride-hailing (I can’t find Slack threads though 🙄 ). I’m not sure if the Product team has anything in their future plans for this. 
* I’d recommend checking in with Anton Diatlov about this - if there’s a proper behaviour tracking system planned for the nearest future, then there’s no point revising the current procedure I think. 
* If there’s no such plans for Product team, then we may take a look at Quentin’s request - but:
** What’s the main reason why he doesn’t want to send even a warning (which isn’t a ban)? I sense that he wants to be a bit easy on his customers, but it’s important to treat all customers fairly. 
** Would you want this to be a market-specific exception, or should this be discussed globally? Essentially, introducing a small FR-specific change here would complicate the (already complicated) process, and also open the gates to other small changes Quentin may suggest in the future. 

I hope this helps 🙂

Hey [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897],

All in all, I agree with your approach but I would advise on giving an advance notice of at least 15 days as well.

Michelle raised a similar question with me a while ago, and this is what we agreed on: 

_Such price changes will not be a de facto change of the general T&Cs because the rates are not included in the terms. However, our global approach is that changes in e.g. commission is part of the T&C updates because the rates and price components are reflected in the app and in driver’s chat. So the following shall apply:_

# _No change of the general T&Cs are required, only update of the rates in the app._
# _Since our approach is that this is an update of terms based on which we provide services to the drivers/riders, we need to follow the notification rules laid out in the P2B Regulation. Such changes to the terms need to be communicated to the business users at least 15 days in advance (Article 3 section 2). Exceptions can be made if (i) we need to do that very urgently and (ii) we are e.g. decreasing the commission which can be seen as a positive change which would make it possible to have a shorter notice period._

_For reference, please see wordings of article 3 section 2 below which applies to changes made in relation to the drivers:_

_Providers of online intermediation services shall notify, on a durable medium, to the business users concerned any proposed changes of their terms and conditions_

_The proposed changes shall not be implemented before the expiry of a notice period which is reasonable and propor tionate to the nature and extent of the envisaged changes and to their consequences for the business user concerned. That notice period shall be at least 15 days from the date on which the provider of online intermediation services notifies the business users concerned about the proposed changes. Providers of online intermediation services shall grant longer notice periods when this is necessary to allow business users to make technical or commercial adaptations to comply with the changes._

SpotDraft doesn’t include a deltas property in the {{CONTRACT_KEY_POINTER_UPDATION}} event payload, making it impossible to see the previous value to verify whether to value was modified. This makes the likelihood of duplicate document uploads highly likely. I have a few workarounds in mind, but that would require a better understanding of the business process.

Hi [~accountid:626c24971a4eb30069d28197], 

Our general assessment remains the same, we should notify the drivers about price changes with a 15 day notification period. This is the general rule and since we are making the assessment that it is to the benefit of the drivers solely based on our internal testing we can’t divert from the general rule without taking certain risks. 

The risk here is that the price changes may be unenforceable if a driver would complain about the price changes and say that they were not duly notified. For example, if the changes are implemented 1 May 2023 and we don’t send out a notification about this then a driver could issue a claim about it and a court could rule that the changes weren’t enforceable until after the required 15 day notification period, i.e. 16 May 2023. If this would be the case then the old price components would still apply to the period between 1 - 15 May 2023 and we would be liable for the incorrect prices during that time. 

However, if you are confident that this will be to the benefit of the drivers then such risk should be quite limited because drivers would not complain about the lack of notification. It is up to the local team to decide if they want to take such risk but from a legal perspective we do have the obligation to notify the drivers 15 days in advance even in this case. As mentioned before the local team may still determine that the risk is worth taking in order to change the components quickly but please ensure that you are comfortable with the potential risks. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hi [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] looping you here in to your view for reg perspective on the topic of the Multiple Stop Feature for Drivers in Romania. 

Are there any obstacles from RO RH legislation to have this feature in RO? 

From the consumer law perspective - the user should be aware and consent to new price. Thanks for your help! 🙏 



*Description:*

We have been asked to review the Multiple Stop Feature for Drivers in every market marked down in this chart [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AxyZTn4SkG_BzS5OJahXGJPAJbskx051ASLlrerouLs/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AxyZTn4SkG_BzS5OJahXGJPAJbskx051ASLlrerouLs/edit#gid=0|smart-link] .

*How the feature works?*

* We want to enable drivers to add stops to the rider journey if so requested by the rider.
* Once rider requests a stop from the driver, driver will add this stop to the driver app.
* Once added, rider will receive a notification that there is an additional stop added to their journey. Please note that rider cannot accept or reject the stop - it is a mere notification (please see a screenshot of what rider sees [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02U62GFQSC/p1667373325003019?thread_ts=1667311149.530179&cid=C02U62GFQSC]).
* Depending on the duration of the stop, the rider will be charged a waiting time fee. The rate of the waiting time fee is displayed before the journey to each rider on a fare card.
* If driver abuses this feature (e.g. adds a stop that was not requested by the rider), the rider will get a refund upon approaching the CS.
* The Figma flow of the feature for better overview may be found here [https://www.figma.com/file/71Pm7c2O6glgFHTpo1PgqL/Multiple-Destinations?t=XY7fKLQrzKuAEcsS-0|https://www.figma.com/file/71Pm7c2O6glgFHTpo1PgqL/Multiple-Destinations?t=XY7fKLQrzKuAEcsS-0|smart-link] . Please reach out to Cliona Dalberg if you don't have access.

*What are the main issues from legal side with this feature?*

* Once driver inputs an additional stop to the app during the ride, rider has no way to consent to this stop in the app.
* Our assumption is that the stop is added by the driver only after it has been requested by the rider during the ride. However, sometimes it might not be the case. Driver may add an additional stop to charge the rider more money without rider's consent. These issues are expected to get resolved by CS.
* Please let the product team know[ in the chart|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AxyZTn4SkG_BzS5OJahXGJPAJbskx051ASLlrerouLs/edit#gid=0] if rider's consent is absolutely necessary under the laws of your market. In this case the feature would be impossible to roll out in your market.
* Please note that similar feature is also rolled out for rider, meaning rider is allowed to input additional stops if necessary. So, the feature for drivers will likely be used in cases where the rider does not want to be charged more for the ride but still wants a stop. As mentioned above, these tensions are expected to be solved by CS.
* Nevertheless, please feel free to flag any other legal issues you may notice with this feature.

Query to get Appsflyer conversions:

{noformat}with installs as (
select date_trunc('quarter', event_date) as m, media_source, 
case when country_code = 'UK' then 'GB' else country_code end as country_code , 
count(*) as installs
from appsflyer.installs 
where app_id = 'ee.mtakso.client'
and platform = 'android'
and media_source in ('googleadwords_int', 'restricted', 'bytedanceglobal_int', 'Apple Search Ads', 'snapchat_int', 'Facebook Ads','Facecook Ads', 'Facecook ads')
and event_date between date('2022-01-01') and date('2023-03-31') 
group by 1,2,3
)
,

first_rides as 
(
select date_trunc('quarter', created_date) as m, attr.media_source as media_source, frac.media_source as media_source_prettified, country.name, upper(country_code) as country_code, count(*) as first_rides
FROM
    ng_public.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user AS ffr
    
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.etl_appsflyer_first_ride_finished AS attr  -- this join is required to connect the table to installs by channel
ON
    ffr.user_id = attr.user_id
left join ng_public.etl_first_ride_attribution_channel frac on ffr.user_id = frac.user_id -- this join is required to get prettified channels

left join admin_system.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.name = ffr.city
left join admin_system.admin_system_country  country on country.code = asc2.country_code -- country code is required to make a join to appsflyer

where created_date between date('2022-01-01') and date('2023-03-31') 
and attr.media_source in ('googleadwords_int', 'restricted', 'bytedanceglobal_int', 'Apple Search Ads', 'snapchat_int', 'Facebook Ads','Facecook Ads', 'Facecook ads')
and frac.platform = 'android'
group by 1,2,3,4,5
)

select i.m as month, i.media_source, media_source_prettified, i.country_code, name as country_name, installs, first_rides
from installs i
left join first_rides 
on i.m = first_rides.m
and i.country_code = first_rides.country_code
and i.media_source = first_rides.media_source
order by first_rides desc{noformat}

*LATVIA*

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?* Yes
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)?* No
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?* No, there is no express presumption of employment. To establish the nature of the legal relationship, it is necessary to assess the nature of the obligations, the essential elements of employment may arise not only from the contract but also from the actual circumstances. A person may submit a claim to a court to recognize the service agreement as an employment contract. Any dispute about the nature of the contract must be settled by the court. Both parties must prove the facts on which they base their claims or objections. 
# *Are RSAs expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* The main characteristic of the employment contract is the submission to the employer’s management and control - the employee complies with the employer’s rules and orders, and working time, whereas the employer ensures fair, safe and healthy working conditions.
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* Yes, up to 2 years
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Couriers / group action / regulators?* Couriers individually. If there are several identical cases against the same defendant, the court can consolidate them into a single proceeding, if it facilitates a more expeditious and correct resolution of the cases. Thus, each courier has to bring an action individually but may ask for his civil cases to be joined with other civil cases involving other couriers. 
Once the Directive is adopted, and after it is transported into the local law, it will become very likely that Labour or Tax authorities would use its ex-officio right to launch investigations into related subjects. The Directive will create a legal presumption of an employment relationship between platforms and persons performing platform work. Member States will be required to establish a framework for effective implementation of the legal presumption through appropriate measures, it will also mean strengthening controls and field inspections.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered couriers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* No. But it is important to note that Latvian tax authority could rely on Article 8(2.2) of Personal income tax law according to which salary taxes must be paid by the company if the natural person (courier) meets at least *one* criterion. Bolt couriers may meet one criterion _“Managed or controlled work, the person is not able to involve their own personnel or use sub-contractors”._ Thus, in practice, LV tax authorities already have a legal ground to claim payment of salary-related taxes, but such discussion/claim never took place in practice. 
Even if the Labour Inspection regards the relationship as non-employment, the tax authorities' assessment is made based on other legal provisions (Article 8(2.2) of Personal income tax) that consider different criteria than the Labour Inspection. Thus, it is possible that LV tax authorities claim payment of salary-related taxes even if under the Labour law the couriers are not considered employees. 
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?* States fees are not high for claims that are not material (around EUR 70), and access to employment litigation is well established. If the court has already established employment relations, further employment-related claims are state fee free.
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all couriers of the platform in a market at once?* No. Court rulings have legal effect only for the parties of the dispute. So no court ruling on reclassification would be automatically applied to all the couriers who were not part of the proceeding. But the effect of a court precedent may trigger similar court actions.

*LITHUANIA*

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?* Yes
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)?* No
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?* There is no express presumption of employment.
# *Are RSAs expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* 
To determine whether a _de facto_ employment relationship is formed, it is examined among other things if the person is under the subordination of the employer, complies with the employer's rules; if the employer takes the risk for the quality and timing of the person’s work. In the case of Bolt couriers there are many other attributes that lean towards civil relations such as the pay of the couriers depends on results, plan their own work time, no workplace is provided. The totality of the circumstances is always assessed. The decision is made based on whether it is more likely that the relationship is in fact of employment.
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* Yes, up to 3 years
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Couriers / group action / regulators?* Couriers. Group action are permitted to defend public interest. However, private parties do not have a possibility to defend the public interest - this may be done only by a prosecutor or another authorized institution.
Once the Directive is adopted, and after it is transported into the local law, it will become very likely that Labour or Tax authorities would use its ex-officio right to launch investigations into related subjects. The Directive will create a legal presumption of an employment relationship between platforms and persons performing platform work. Member States will be required to establish a framework for effective implementation of the legal presumption through appropriate measures, it will also mean strengthening controls and field inspections.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered couriers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* No
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*  Access to employment litigation is well established. If the court has established employment relations, further employment-related claims are state fee free.
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all couriers of the platform in a market at once?* No. Court rulings have legal effect only for the parties of the dispute. So no court ruling on reclassification would be automatically applied to all the couriers who were not part of the proceeding. But the effect of a court precedent may trigger similar court actions.

Hey! From the legal end it’s rather straightforward - regardless of the invoicing setup (intermediary or “resale”) it’s the end user who remains the recipient of the transportation service and is bound by the Rides T&C’s, see foremost 1.2, 2.6, 5.4 in our [template|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BS8VUWyJekCexkDFTAKopqNeYu1QvPwUMR8NdW2b5-0/edit].

“Resale” is only used in the context of tax (VAT) laws here having no meaningful implications on the civil law or regulatory qualification of the matter - as far as we are concerned the API partner does not become a reseller (in other meanings of the word than tax that is) due to the mere fact that it’s aggregating invoices from different drivers/fleets and then issuing one single invoice in its own name. _Taxes are reported and paid AS IF it was resale though - based on article 28 EU VAT Directive, a tax fiction is created that drivers provided transport services to the partner, who then provided the same services to users._

From that angle [~accountid:60b2030ffe01e80069c64f5f] the intermediary invoicing setup you are suggesting here is even more straightforward than the “resale” one we have been using as default for the API deals.

Thanks Marilin. just for the completeness, sharing the feedback from Sorina:

* We have some specific examples from our experience with Fiscal and Labour agencies. Many fleets choose to collaborate with drivers/couriers with *PFA* contract (authorised natural persons) to reduce the costs with the taxes. The labour authorities decided, during controls, that the relationships between the fleets and the drivers/couriers were in reality one of work (employment). They can apply fines of 20,000 lei for each person identified in this situation (up to a maximum of 200,000 lei) and even order the suspension of the activity of the workplace subject to control, until the situation is remedied. Labour inspectors can also compel the company to conclude employment contracts. Both RH and Delivery work with fleets, so the responsibility falls with the fleets. RH can also work directly with PFA, because the RH law allows that. Food delivery is not regulated by any law, so there is always a risk when working directly with couriers, and not via fleets. 
* Fiscal Authority has stated officially (media statements) that was a systemic risk in the platform work, because the fleets do not correctly register the employment contracts with the drivers/couriers. The President of the Fiscal Agency also stated that all the work was done in collaboration with platforms, who put at their disposal info on the fleets and drivers/couriers' activity. Fiscal Agency informed the controls would continue this year.

Hi [~accountid:5c2f512d36647b5b91017d0c] 

Thank you so much for raising this question. I truly appreciate in looping me in and asking upfront. There are certain intertwined aspects to your query that I would like to clarify.



*IP related problems*

# AI generated images are not protected by copyright (copyright protects works made by humans), meaning that if we use such images and somebody copies us, there is no copyright infringement and we cannot request the “infringer” to cease the use of a copy;
# Images made by humans that incorporate AI-produced images can be protected;
# AI models could potentially create new images that “mirror” an original work (imitation) or the style of the author of the original work (derivative work), leading to risks of copyright infringement.
# [class-action lawsuit for copyright infringement against|https://stablediffusionlitigation.com/pdf/00201/1-1-stable-diffusion-complaint.pdf] Midjourney and other AI image creating companies has been filed in the US. According to the plaintiffs the use of their copyright protected images in the training of Stable Diffusion (AI Image product that Midjourney uses to train its program and create images) amounts to copyright infringement. In addition, the plaintiffs claim that AI images can be created in the "style of" a specific author thereby profiting off the author’s distinct artistic identities which are uniquely associated with the author.

*Bolt externally facing terms and conditions*

Depending on the use case, we may need to adjust our externally facing terms and conditions as well as privacy terms. Legislation foresee informing consumers of using AI generated content or informing (in certain cases obtaining prior opt-in) for using AI. 

*Review of Midjourney user terms*

Please note, that for using Midjourney in our work, we must purchase a “Pro” membership ([see T&C|https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/terms-of-service]). Using the non-Pro version by companies our size is not allowed by the terms. Prior to use, we need to review T&C’s (legal team) and privacy terms (privacy team) together with any InfoSec implications (InfoSec team). Please note that we have not done this yet.

*One system at the time*

We are exploring to use ChatGPT API version in Bolt for certain cases. Thus, it is not reasonable to start purchasing other service providers besides that. Let’s concentrate on using and developing consciously and thoughtfully one system for our actual needs and see how much benefit we can get from it before jumping into any other system.

[~accountid:5c6bbd9d00a665752ca2c9e8] from the Data Science team is the +gatekeeper for any desire to use AI within Bolt+. Should you have a use-case where use of AI could benefit the company, then please send your request with a short description directly to Siim.

*Internal AI policy on its way.*

Finally, please note that the AI task force led by Siim, is developing our internal policy on Acceptable Use of AI to ensure that we can benefit the most from emerging service providers.   



Please reach out should you have any further questions on this matter, and do please inform me or Siim of any interesting findings or possibilities that MRK team may see - this is truly interesting journey we are on, and it is good to explore this with full (task-)force and our best knowledge 😊

Objective is to determine legal framework around window shopping (price and ETA extractions) for specific country. Here is the methodology we launched : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|smart-link] There is also section about legal risk in the methodology. For determining the legal framework the legal council should do following:

* Country legal council  uses [+Legal questionnaire+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-ZjNVX9rtsXA4IWpYt5PR3RVGLfNBY46OdpE7JGvy5g/edit] and checks following: 
** criminal punishment scope for specific country
** civil punishment scope for specific country 
** competitor T&C review
** etc
* Country legal council uses answers to questionnaire to define punishment scope for each window shopping scenario in the [+global risk matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_eWb4mN9Nph8g1OuD0urnNoYmaPGjHEwlKYIMw3KfCU/edit]:
** Punishment scope will be considered every time. But if the  likelihood of the risk materializing is *LOW* than we will not ask about punishment.

*Valletta’s approach to find out sensitivity coefficients:*

Problem: for Valletta we don’t have good periods when weather and fleet were fixed, just price was changing. We could have reusred coefficients from another city, but Valletta is a touristic destination, and tourists may have another price sensitivity. 

But, we can find a period when price was fixed, weather was stable and only fleet was changing. This way we find out relationship between fleet and users. {code:sql} SELECT
	k.key,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) AS count_of_users,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
	SUM(k.order_price) AS sum_of_in_app_orders_eur,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
	SUM(k.fraud_amount) AS sum_of_fraud_payments_eur,
	(COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.0)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
	(SUM(k.fraud_amount) * 1.0) / SUM(k.order_price) AS fraud_payment_sum_ratio
FROM
	(
	SELECT
		etl.order_id AS orders_id,
		etl.user_price_eur AS order_price,
		etl.card_bin AS card_bin,
		etl.card_bin || ':' || etl.country_code AS KEY,
		etl.country_code AS country_code,
		etl.user_id AS user_id,
		CASE
			WHEN etl.is_chargeback
			OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id
			ELSE NULL
		END AS fraud_payments,
		CASE
			WHEN etl.is_chargeback
			OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.user_price_eur
			ELSE NULL
		END AS fraud_amount
	FROM
		ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
	WHERE
		etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
		AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
		AND etl.created >= DATEADD(month, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
		AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(month, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
                ) AS k
GROUP BY
	1
HAVING
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) > 20
	AND COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) > 5
	AND SUM(k.fraud_amount) > 300
	AND
               (
               (COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) > 0.4)
		OR
               (SUM(k.fraud_amount) * 1.0) / SUM(k.order_price) > 0.4

Ok, so the root cause for this is that the table is created by Spark, but read by Presto. They both need different metadata to understand which files belong to a table, and this metadata is currently not always updated in a fully transactional way. Therefore this error may happen after every update to the table if those updates are not done carefully.

The reason why the error sometimes only appears on some Presto clusters but not on others, is that the clusters cache the table metadata, which can lead to additional inconsistencies after updates.

To mitigate this:

* in the long term, we will unify the table metadata used by Spark and Presto, which will completely avoid this problem. this relies on some yet-to-be-developed features in Spark and Presto though. so it’s not feasible to happen immediately, and we also have no ETA yet.
* in the meantime, we try to limit the different ways how tables are created, since this error happens a lot more frequently if the update process is not carefully updating the metadata. is the mentioned table updated via dbt? there should be a macro to update symlinks (the table metadata for Presto) that is called after runs, maybe it’s missing for this model?
* we additionally periodically run a separate health check to detect and fix such cases where metadata is out of sync. i can see that for the mentioned table this happened 12 times over the last two weeks, which is probably the reason why the issue here fixed itself.

Objective is to determine legal framework around window shopping (price and ETA extractions) for specific country. For determining the legal framework the legal council should do following:

* Country legal council  uses [+Legal questionnaire+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-ZjNVX9rtsXA4IWpYt5PR3RVGLfNBY46OdpE7JGvy5g/edit] and checks following: 
** criminal punishment scope for specific country
** civil punishment scope for specific country 
** competitor T&C review
** etc
* Country legal council uses answers to questionnaire to define punishment scope for each window shopping scenario in the [+global risk matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_eWb4mN9Nph8g1OuD0urnNoYmaPGjHEwlKYIMw3KfCU/edit]:

The app can ask for mic permission when it’s active, but if device was locked and user answered the call through system call UI we can’t ask for mic permission so we have 3 possible solutions:

For example, we may challenge and send them through 3DS verification if we determine irregular activities. Hence, in the end, we should look at the bigger picture instead of user per user. {noformat}#!/bin/sh

. ./_base.sh
. ./$(basename $0 ".sh").argv

start=$seconds
limit=${argv_limit:-5000}
echo argv_mysql_env: ${argv_mysql_env}
echo argv_mysql_username: ${argv_mysql_username}
echo argv_mysql_database: ${argv_mysql_database}
echo argv_mysql_username: ${argv_mysql_username}

output_file="$1_${argv_mysql_env}"
if [ -z "$1" ]; then
  echo "No output file prefix"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "${output_file}.tsv" ]; then
  check_mysql
  set_mysql_args

  log "${mysql_host} $ Check mysql ROUTE READONLY=1 hostname..."
  mysql --host=${mysql_host} --port=${mysql_port} --user=${mysql_username} --password=${mysql_password} ${mysql_database} -c -s << EOF 2>${output_file}.mysql.err |  while IFS='' read l; do log "${mysql_host} $ $l"; done
    SELECT /* ROUTE READONLY=1 */ @@HOSTNAME;
EOF
  set_mysql_errors ${output_file}.mysql.err
  if [ "${mysql_errors}" -gt "0" ]; then
    err "Fail"
    exit 1
  fi

  log "${mysql_host} $ Query data from mysql..."
  mysql --host=${mysql_host} --port=${mysql_port} --user=${mysql_username} --password=${mysql_password} ${mysql_database} -c -s << EOF 1>${output_file}.tsv 2>${output_file}.mysql.err
    SELECT /* ROUTE READONLY=1 */
      pmu_po.id as po_card_id,
      pmu.expires as adyen_card_expiry,
      pmu_po.expires as po_card_expiry
    FROM payment_method_user pmu
      INNER JOIN payment_method_user pmu_po ON pmu_po.payment_user_id = pmu.payment_user_id
        AND pmu_po.payment_method_type = 'processout'
        AND pmu_po.card_last4 = pmu.card_last4
        AND pmu_po.card_bin = pmu.card_bin
        AND pmu_po.is_deleted = 0
        AND pmu_po.expires < pmu.expires
    WHERE pmu.payment_method_type = 'adyen'
      AND pmu.is_deleted = 0
      AND pmu.expires > CURRENT_DATE
EOF
  set_mysql_errors ${output_file}.mysql.err
  save_mysql_credentials
  if [ "${mysql_errors}" -gt "0" ]; then
    rm ${output_file}.tsv
    err "Fail"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

cards_count=$(($(cat ${output_file}.tsv | wc -l)))

log "Split ${cards_count} data per ${limit} rows in one file..."
rm -rf ${output_file}__s*
split -d -l ${limit} -a 4 ${output_file}.tsv ${output_file}__s

files_count=$(($(ls -1 ${output_file}__s* | wc -l)))
f_no=0

log "Generating SQL updates for ${files_count} files..."
sql_script_list=""
for f in $(ls -1 ${output_file}__s*); do
  f_no=$((f_no+1))
  cat $f | while read po_card_id adyen_card_expiry po_card_expiry; do echo "UPDATE payment_method_user set expires = DATE(\"$adyen_card_expiry\") WHERE id = $po_card_id AND expires = DATE(\"$po_card_expiry\");"; 
  done > $f.sql
  rm -rf $f
  sql_script_list+="$f.sql "
done

echo "$sql_script_list"
./execute-sqls.sh -e $argv_mysql_env -u $argv_mysql_username -d $argv_mysql_database $sql_script_list;

log "Done"
exit 0{noformat}

Discussed Women Driver Conversion Lift with Google. 

Decided that it’s not the best idea for such a campaign, here’s why:

# It’s only possible to have 30% control group and no opportunity to regulate it. 30% is something that *prevents* us from *obtaining maximal reach* (which is one of the goals).
# Since the campaign is a ‘Reach' one, it’s possible that we will have *network effect* with high probability of control group still seeing the ad or hearing about it somehow. The following factors increase this probability:
## We will be advertising on all the devices, but splitting to A and B is possible only on device level. So a user can be *simultaneously* *be in test and control group* given that he has *multiple devices*.
## There are *issues following the same user* via the cookies (which is mentioned below).
# Control group might not be very clean due to tracking on web.
## There are browsers updating cookies every 24 hours (no opportunity to track users on desktop) (One solution could be to do enhanced conversion (those based on user id), but we still do not have them)
## For YT it’s most probably not possible to check post-view conversions (which is crucial for this experiment)


One idea why I was thinking about an experiment with Google is that they could help us identify the uplift for women exclusively (since google has some knowledge on a user’s gender).

However, we discussed that this most probably will not help, because campaign will exclusively be targeted on women.

So if a person sees the ad, it is already defined as a woman by Google and there’s no reason to identify gender while doing the test. (In other words - we do not have to separate men and women for analysis, since the whole population of test participants is women (as identified by Google) by default).

P.S. FYI: In another ticket, we have informed Ads team of the following: 

*IP related problems*

# AI generated images are not protected by copyright (copyright protects works made by humans), meaning that if we use such images and somebody copies us, there is no copyright infringement and we cannot request the “infringer” to cease the use of a copy;
# Images made by humans that incorporate AI-produced images can be protected;
# AI models could potentially create new images that “mirror” an original work (imitation) or the style of the author of the original work (derivative work), leading to risks of copyright infringement.
# [class-action lawsuit for copyright infringement against|https://stablediffusionlitigation.com/pdf/00201/1-1-stable-diffusion-complaint.pdf] Midjourney and other AI image creating companies has been filed in the US. According to the plaintiffs the use of their copyright protected images in the training of Stable Diffusion (AI Image product that Midjourney uses to train its program and create images) amounts to copyright infringement. In addition, the plaintiffs claim that AI images can be created in the "style of" a specific author thereby profiting off the author’s distinct artistic identities which are uniquely associated with the author.

*Bolt externally facing terms and conditions*

Depending on the use case, we may need to adjust our externally facing terms and conditions as well as privacy terms. Legislation foresee informing consumers of using AI generated content or informing (in certain cases obtaining prior opt-in) for using AI.

*Review of Midjourney user terms*

Please note, that for using Midjourney in our work, we must purchase a “Pro” membership ([see T&C|https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/terms-of-service]). Using the non-Pro version by companies our size is not allowed by the terms. Prior to use, we need to review T&C’s (legal team) and privacy terms (privacy team) together with any InfoSec implications (InfoSec team). Please note that we have not done this yet.

*One system at the time*

We are exploring to use ChatGPT API version in Bolt for certain cases. Thus, it is not reasonable to start purchasing other service providers besides that. Let’s concentrate on using and developing consciously and thoughtfully one system for our actual needs and see how much benefit we can get from it before jumping into any other system.

*Internal AI policy on its way.*

Finally, please note that the AI task force led by Data Science team, is developing our internal policy on Acceptable Use of AI to ensure that we can benefit the most from emerging service providers.

Thank you for this additional context. From privacy perspective having in-cabin monitoring would be deemed highly privacy-intrusive. Video recording is also currently one of the main topics of interest of our lead data protection supervisory authority (AKI).

I see two main issues that may be concerning from GDPR point of view:

*1. Data minimisation* 

According to the GDPR, the scope of data processed should be strictly limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed. If this footage is not necessarily needed from Bolt’s side, then the recording can be deemed as unlawful just based on this premise.

Is there an operational and technical possibility that this footage wouldn’t be accessible to Bolt? 

If the recording can be turned off then, I’d suggest adding a sticker on/near the cabin-facing cameras saying that the camera is not operating (the Estonian data protection supervisory authority has stated that even if it is a replica of a camera or a camera not filming, the person would still assume that they are being filmed, so it should be appropriately marked).

*2. Legal basis*

Under GDPR, each processing activity needs to have a legal basis from the exhaustive list of possible legal grounds included in article 6. If, from the business perspective, Bolt would like to pursue in-cabin monitoring, then only possible legal grounds for such process are either legitimate interest or consent- and both of them, given the circumstances, may still be challenged by the regulator.

* Legitimate interest

GDPR allows the processing when it is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller. Generally speaking, protecting controller’s assets could be classified as such an interest. However, GDPR is very clear that it doesn’t relate to the processing where such interests are overridden by the interests or fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject (in particular when the data subject is a child). In my view it is very likely that it would be contested by the regulator, given the imbalance of the interests. Drivers renting a car can reasonably expect for the car to be a private space and this recording could be deemed very intrusive. Also, as GDPR specifically refers to children data as a factor that may prevent data controllers from relying on legitimate interest, in this specific scenario we cannot exclude the possibility that the cameras will capture the footage of children traveling in the car.

* Consent

The second option would be for Bolt to rely on the client's consent to proceed with the processing - it should be granted by the client prior to the processing, so ideally before the car is rented out. Please note however, that one of the conditions for a valid consent under GDPR is that it has to be voluntary, so there is a risk of that aspect being challenged by the regulator.



In any case, regardless of the legal basis, the data subject should be also informed about such monitoring, so I’d also strongly suggest adding additional stickers in the car informing the driver that the inside of the cabin is monitored.





In summary, from privacy perspective, in-cabin recording is not recommended, however if the business decision will be made to proceed - please let me know, so we can discuss potential mitigation measures.

hi [~accountid:60803758f74b3f006a35b6bb], there are more or less two options:

# you configure new ingestions for the new tables, following [this guide|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4049731679/Data+Lake+MySQL+TiDB+Ingestion+API]. analysts will need to migrate queries.
# you change the [source for existing ingestions|https://github.com/bolteu/change-data-capture/blob/787a09947a69e2abb5977527dcee63a88c1fc226/src/ingestion_config/ng/live/fleet-2.json#L204] without renaming the target tables. nobody will need to migrate queries, but a year from now someone may look at the ingestion config and wonder why it’s using wrong table names.

i would probably suggest to go with option 2 here.

if we merge the config switch for the ingestion source within less than 7 days after renaming the table (retention period in Kafka), it should continue without any gaps in the replicated data. worst case we would have to [add a backfill|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4049731679/Data+Lake+MySQL+TiDB+Ingestion+API#If-you-need-to-backfill-a-table] for the gap.

between renaming the table and updating the ingestion config no data will be replicated though, so if stakeholders need this data for reports the config update should probably happen rather soonish after renaming the table.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] below are my answers for FR and BE. 

*FRANCE:* 

From a purely legal standpoint, in order to mitigate the reclass risk (and walking away from the “wearing a uniform” impression) branding needs to be considered as advertising services provided by the driver and paid by Bolt.

*Consideration consists of* +*2 components:*+

# *Flat compensation* of 100 EUROS paid monthly for the previous month - *not correlated to KPIs.* 

From a tax standpoint, this should be treated as *advertising* as per your categorisation. 



2. *back commission* of 8% of price of the ride which is paid back to the driver. - *connected to KPIs but applied to any ride (no minimum number of rides required).*

From a tax standpoint, this should be treated as *a campaign*  as per your categorisation. 

For the legal requirements I refer you to this document prepared with [~accountid:616fd1373e3753006f97f319] [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yxBarCT4KHlAZSY-4SrpXY2uUamTRiHU/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yxBarCT4KHlAZSY-4SrpXY2uUamTRiHU/edit|smart-link]  



*BELGIUM:*  

That current RH law in Belgium bans ads on vehicles, at least until an implementing decree/official authorisation will be issued. *The law only authorises the displaying of affiliations signs, i.e. logos of intermediary platforms used by the driver.*After checking with OC BE, we had to reconsider our approach to Branding in BE to prevent it from being caught in the scope of law banning advertising.  *Branding BE must be rather perceived as a mere displaying of the "*+*affiliation sign" as referred to in the law and to reduce the reclass risks consideration is not connected to KPIs.*+

Therefore, pursuant to your categorisation, from a tax standpoint branding should be treated *as advertising. However,* please note that from a regulatory/ legal perspective advertising is not yet authorised for RH and we need to avoid any reference to advertising services in the invoices or any other output. 

Please let me know if you need further clarification. 

Michela

Hi all 

A few points from a DAC7 perspective: 

* A “Seller” means a platform user that is registered on the platform and carries out a relevant activity (i.e. passenger transport services in this case). Whilst the old company remains registered on the platform, technically it is not carrying out the relevant activity. That said, on the basis that we were not aware of the company being closed and have in good faith assumed based on their agreement to the T&Cs that they are carrying out the relevant activity, I would continue to consider the old company as a Seller for DAC7 purposes. 
* We must, inter alia, report all IBANs and the names of the holders of such IBANs used for payouts as part of the DAC7. Validating IBANs and their holders is not required under the DAC7. This means that all income earned by such companies - old or new - will be pulled into the DAC7 report. The FR tax authorities can then challenge the income earned and reported by the driver / fleet as needed. 
* We must carry out regular due diligence checks at least every 36 months for each Seller, unless we have a reason to believe that the information initially collected is not correct. It may be arguable that the driver / fleet was obliged to notify us of the changes under the T&Cs (if applicable), albeit we might nevertheless face challenges on our overall processes and quality as a platform operator. 
* There are two types of fines under the Estonian tax law applicable in the context of DAC7: (i) €3,300 for not submitting a DAC7 report at all, and (ii) obstruction of activities of tax authority (to include e.g. failure to comply with the requirements for the keeping of records) of €3,200 per act. It’s unclear if the latter applies per driver / fleet or the overall quality of the data included in the report. We’d be hopeful that it’s the latter, but it’s not evident based on the wording of the law or legislative guidance.   

Many thanks

Tiiu

[~accountid:5e4fb22d2a59dc0c8fe5905d] [~accountid:5b3cc136d394412e188f155e] Hey! 🙂 Guilherme (the ticket requester) from the Fraud team asked if we may consider creating a short training to help CS agents recognise the driver fraud cases described below. I’ve finished drafting the required KB article updates and will publish them today.

What do you think about creating a training? Do you need additional information in order to make the decision? 

----

_context_

*Issue reported by the Fraud team*

* The Fraud team discovered a driver fraud scenario when the driver takes a very long route or goes to a very far destination but hasn’t logged the trip destination changes in the app. These are the typical telling signs:
** Estimated trip distance and duration is very short
** Actual trip distance driven and duration are significantly longer
** Driver didn’t adjust the trip destination in the app
* Such drivers report that the customer paid less. They may have submitted a price review or simply reached out to CS reporting that customers paid less than they should have.
* If such a case is discovered, agents shouldn’t adjust the final order price - instead, they should educate the driver to always adjust the trip destination in the app. Additionally, no compensation should be provided here.
* In the UK alone, CS doesn’t recognise these cases as driver fraud and adjusts the price, causing significant losses (CS adjust the order price, the rider payment fails and we have to compensate drivers).
* The UK CS team has been informed ([thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CM30FTRHP/p1681130605527859] on #uk_updates) about recognising these cases; however, CS still make mistakes. 
* The Fraud team wants to enforce this as a global procedure (to prevent this case of driver fraud).
* There are two KB articles affected (I’ve already drafted the process changes and will publish them today):
** 🚗 [Completing a Price Review|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013391799--Completing-a-Price-Review] (agents may discover these driver fraud cases when completing price reviews)
** 🚗 [Driver reporting undercharged or offline ride|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360010166173--Driver-reporting-undercharged-or-offline-ride] (driver may report this issue and not request a price review, or the market may not have price reviews enabled)

Hey [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], please see below the research re Azerbaijan. Please let me know if you have any questions re this.

----

*_Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? Yes/no_*

Yes.

The Labor Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (the *“Labor Code”*) defines the employment relations as the fulfillment (in person) of the labor functions of the profession or position for which the person was hired (appointed), elected, reinstated at the workplace determined on the basis of mutual agreement with the employer in accordance with the obligations stipulated in the labor legislation, collective agreements and employment agreement for a salary, observation by the employee of the internal disciplinary rules, guarantee of working conditions, benefits and labor protection by the employer and obeyance of other principles specified in the Labor Code.

Accordingly, employment relations are relations based on (1) the personal discharge, according to obligations provided for by the employment law and collective bargaining agreements and pacts, by an employee for a salary compensation of a job function of a profession or position at the workplace determined based on a mutual agreement with an employer, for which he/she was hired (appointed), elected, reinstated, (ii) his/her observance of internal disciplinary rules, (iii) provision by the employer of the employee’s working conditions, guarantees, and labor protection, (iv) as well as the principles of the Code.

Moreover, the following relations are considered employment relations and cannot be formalized by civil law agreements:

* if the content of the agreement complies with the requirements of Sub-Section 43.2 and the form of the agreement is made in accordance with the form provided by Sub-Section 44.3 of the Labor Code;
* when the labor book is submitted to formalize the relations between the parties;
* when the relations between the parties arise in connection with the admission (appointment) to a relevant profession or position, including paid elective or appointment, as well as holding a position based on a competition, employment on a quota, reinstatement by a court decision;
* if the relations between the parties arise in connection with the performance of works (services) related to the main field of activity of the employer;
* if the relations between the parties arise in connection with the performance of works (services) in the order of replacement or temporary replacement;
* when the provisions of the temporary labor contract apply to the extension of the contract in case if the work (service) is of a temporary nature due to the conditions of its performance;
* when the composition of the fee paid for the performed work (service) consists of the monthly tariff (position) salary, allowance, and bonus; and
* if the agreement provides for the regulation of issues provided for in Sections 10 (employee’s job duties), 77 (severance during termination), 112 (annual leave), 179 (maintenance of work place and average salary) and 186 (disciplinary liability) of the Labor Code.

*_Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)._*

We have not come across any publicly available evidence.

*_Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? Yes/no_*

Yes, employment relations can be presumed in cases mentioned in response to question 1 and do not need to always be proved by the individual.  The competent state authority (MLSPP (defined below) or a prosecutor’s office (for engaging more than ten persons)) may initiate the investigation based on the application of a person or information received from another source (for instance, mass media).

*_Are reclassification sensitive activities expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?_*

Yes.  Please refer to our answer to question 1.   

*_Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e., for previously withheld earnings?)_*

Yes; a person can claim employment relations and the related benefits.  In accordance with the Civil Procedural Code, each party must prove the circumstances he/she refers to as the basis of his/her claims and objections.  In case if the plaintiff fails to prove the actual amount of salary he/she is entitled to, the court is likely to calculate the salary (as well as unpaid vacations) based on the minimum wage applied in the relevant periods (AZN 345 (approx. EUR 185) as of 1 January 2023). 

*_Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators_*

Under the Civil Procedural Code, all individuals and legal entities have the right to use court protection in accordance with the law in order to protect and secure their rights and freedoms, as well as their interests.

Accordingly, drivers can take a court action against Bolt individually or as a group.

Moreover, drivers may appeal to the _Ministry_ of Labor _and_ Social Protection of _Population_ of the Republic of Azerbaijan (“MLSPP”).  If MLSPP establishes that the employer hires employees without entering a labor contract with the latter, it prepares a protocol on administrative violation and issues a decision based on the protocol.  If the entity fails to pay the fine within ten days of the date of the protocol, the protocol is sent to court within one day for consideration. 

MLSPP’s powers are limited to the imposition of fines for the administrative breach and do not embrace the power of reclassification.   

Under the Code of Administrative Violations, for engaging an individual in performance of services/works without concluding an employment agreement, the legal entity is subject to an administrative fine in the amount of AZN20,000-25,000 (approx. EUR 10,700-13,400).

Under the Criminal Code, for engaging ten or more persons in performance of services/works without concluding employment agreements with them, the officials of a legal entity are subject to penalty in the amount of AZN7,000-10,000 (approx. EUR 3,700-5,350) or correction works for up to two years or restriction of freedom for up to two years or an imprisonment for up to two years.

*_Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?_*

To the best of our knowledge, no.

*_What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?_*

Before filing a suit with the court, the party to an employment dispute must participate in an initial mediation session.  The party applying for mediation needs to pay an initial mediation fee of AZN50.  If parties decide to discontinue the mediation, the mediator issues a letter, which serves as a basis for an application to court.

The state fees for the claims change depending on the claim amount and are as follows:

* AZN30, when the claim amount is up to AZN1,000;
* AZN30 + one percent of the claim amount above AZN1,000, when the claim amount is from AZN1,000 to AZN10,000;
* AZN120 + 0.3 percent of the claim amount above AZN10,000, when the claim amount is from AZN10,000 to AZN100,000;
* AZN390 + 0.1 percent of the claim amount above AZN100,000, when the claim amount is from AZN100,000 to AZN1,000,000;
* AZN1,290 + 0.05 percent of the claim amount above AZN1,000,000 (not exceeding AZN50,000 in each case), when the claim price exceeds AZN1,000,000; and
* AZN100 for claims without any value.

There is no requirement to engage an attorney in the first instance or appellate courts, i.e., the person can represent himself.  The engagement of an attorney at the cassation instance is required.  

The statute of limitations for claiming damages arising out of employment relations is one year from the moment the person becomes aware of the breach of his/her rights.   

The level of access to justice for individuals is high in Azerbaijan.  It is also worth mentioning that Azerbaijani laws are mostly employee friendly.

*_Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?_*

Subject to the below, no.

Under Sub-Section 51.1 of the Civil Procedural Code, a lawsuit can be brought jointly by several plaintiffs or against several defendants.  Each of the plaintiffs or defendants acts in the proceedings independently against the opposite party. 

Joint participants can entrust the conduct of legal proceedings to one of the participants.  Accordingly, all drivers may entrust their representation to one person (which is practically hard).

The court would consider the circumstances of each driver independently; however, in the end there will be one decision which reflects the parts related to each party (if, the claims have some differences) or which affirms/denies the joint claim (if, the claims are identical).

* AZN30 + one percent of the claim amount above AZN1,000, when the claim amount is from AZN1,000 to AZN10,000;
* AZN120 + 0.3 percent of the claim amount above AZN10,000, when the claim amount is from AZN10,000 to AZN100,000;
* AZN390 + 0.1 percent of the claim amount above AZN100,000, when the claim amount is from AZN100,000 to AZN1,000,000;
* AZN1,290 + 0.05 percent of the claim amount above AZN1,000,000 (not exceeding AZN50,000 in each case), when the claim price exceeds AZN1,000,000; and
* AZN100 for claims without any value.

There is no requirement to engage an attorney in the first instance or appellate courts, i.e., the person can represent himself.  The engagement of an attorney at the cassation instance is required. 

The statute of limitations for claiming damages arising out of employment relations is one year from the moment the person becomes aware of the breach of his/her rights.    

The level of access to justice for individuals is high in Azerbaijan.  It is also worth mentioning that Azerbaijani laws are mostly employee friendly.

*_Can claims be made to reclassify all couriers of the platform in a market at once?_*

Subject to the below, no.

Under Sub-Section 51.1 of the Civil Procedural Code, a lawsuit can be brought jointly by several plaintiffs or against several defendants.  Each of the plaintiffs or defendants acts in the proceedings independently against the opposite party. 

Joint participants can entrust the conduct of legal proceedings to one of the participants.  Accordingly, all couriers may entrust their representation to one person (which is practically hard).  The court would consider the circumstances of each courier independently; however, in the end there will be one decision which reflects the parts related to each party (if, the claims have some differences) or which affirms/denies the joint claim (if, the claims are identical).

In Finland they categorise electric personal transportation devices into 3 areas:

# Devices to assist/replace walking
# Light electric vehicles
# Bicycles (electric assisted and motorised)

If the maximum speed and power of the Bolt scooter is 15 km/h and 1 kW.  In Finland, they class this type of vehicle as a Device to assist/replace walking. This type of device does not require an indicator.

If the maximum speed and power of the Bolt scooter is 16–25 km/h and 1 kW. In Finland they class this type of vehicle as Light electric vehicles. This type of device does not require an indicator however does require a front light, reflector at the back (must be used in dark and dusk, both may be worn by the driver) and a sound signalling device.
