Hello [~accountid:623db04fee1b5a00702a0ea0] , 

Thank you for your ticket. 

* {{Driver Threatens to Physically Harm Rider}} -> driver makes a *threat* of physical harm passenger. 
** If the driver makes any other type of threat, then it could be covered by other ECs. For example: 
*** {{Driver Threatens Terrorist Activity}} - a generic threat to public safety motivated by a political, religious, racial, or ideological cause
*** {{Driver Displays Road Rage}} -a _violent outburst of road rage against other drivers or road conditions (i.e. aggressive speech against other motorists, rude hand gestures, a verbal altercation with other drivers)._
*** {{Threat to Bolt or Employees}} - threat specifically targeting Bolt and/or its employees as described on this page.
* {{Driver Physically Assaults or Attempts to Assault Individual(s)}} -> different situations here, where there is a real or attempted physical assault.  
* {{Rider Threatens to Physically Harm Driver}} and {{Driver and Rider Physically Assaults or Attempts to Assault Driver}} refer both only to drivers.  
** If a passenger threatens or assaults a third party, this would be a {{Non-platform Safeguarding}} case. 

Hope it’s clear, but if you have any other questions, please just let me know. 

Thank you and have a good day, 

Alessandro

Hi Andrei

After conducting a review of the agreement, I have identified several risks, primarily of a commercial nature, that you may wish to consider addressing before signing. However, from a legal perspective, it is acceptable to proceed with signing the agreement without addressing these risks, provided that they are acknowledged and assessed internally, and it is determined that it is not necessary to renegotiate the terms of the agreement. 

* Clause 2.9 - Bolt has 15 days from receipt of the service to notify VISA is it’s not satisfied with the quality of the services. If Bolt fails to notify VISA of any errors within 15 days, Bolt shall be deemed to have accepted the services (no more disputes).
* Clause 7.5 - only VISA has a right to terminate the agreement for convenience giving 60 days notice. Bolt has no corresponding right (i.e. the agreement can only be terminated if VISA commits a material breach etc). Please consider adding a mutual termination right.
* Clause 9.4.2. Dispute resolution venue: Arbitration in Dubai (that is likely very expensive). Please consider proposing a neutral less expensive applicable law and jurisdiction - e.g. applicable law: England and Wales, applicable jurisdiction: Courts of England. Not necessary if you are confident in the provider and the fact that no dispute will occur.
* Clause 9.6 - problematic and potentially excessive - please consider whether Bolt we should request that the following clause 9.6. is removed. If you decide not to request the removal of clause 9.6, please consider requesting that the clause is made mutual: _9.6. During the term of this Agreement and for twelve months thereafter, the Client shall allow Visa or its designated agent to perform audits of the Client’s records relating to the subject matter of this Agreement to determine whether the Client is in compliance with this Agreement. The client shall also provide Visa or its designated agent during normal business hours with books, records and supporting documentation to perform any such audit during normal business hours._
* Clauses 3.3 and 3.4 of Appendix 1: NB! VISA keeps all intellectual property rights to the services and licenses the Deliverables to Bolt only for the purpose of internal use - are we OK with the fact that VISA keeps the IP rights, what does it potentially mean - can they sell the Deliverables also to 3rd parties, are we OK with the fact that the Deliverables can be used by us for internal purposes only?  _3.3. Visa will own all Intellectual Property Rights in or pertaining to all Deliverables and other materials developed by Visa in the course of providing the Consulting Services._
* Clause 5.2 - Services and Deliverables are provided ‘as is’, i.e. Visa makes no other warranty, whether written or oral, is expressed or implied and Visa specifically disclaims the implied warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose.
* *Clause 6.3/ 6.3  VISA excludes all liability for the consulting services, except the breach of confidentiality obligation. This is a significant risk - Bolt will have no remedies if the services do not meet the expected quality or VISA causes damage to Bolt by breaching the agreement (other than a breach of consultancy obligation). lease consider whether there are any hidden risks - e.g. whether VISA could be breaching third-party intellectual property rights (that might make Bolt subject of a dispute with a 3rd party), if yes, we should add relevant warranties and indemnities in the agreement.* Please also consider requesting VISA that the exclusion of liability clauses are made mutual (necessary if there’s a risk that Bolt will cause VISA damages under this Agreement - this might be an unlikely scenario). P
* Clause 7.4. - add Bolt contact for notices.
* Appendix 2 - Territory missing.
* Appendix 2 - description of services is pretty vague considering the fee and the fact that it’s an annual fee - please consider making the description more specific, incl. agreed on timelines/ deadlines, etc.
* Annex 2 - Client’s Obligations - please add ‘number of working days’ in the following clause: _The Client will submit to Visa within [insert term] working days of signing this Project Plan the data necessary for further analysis. Within [insert term] working days of receipt Visa will validate the completeness and integrity of the data and will confirm the Project start date or will revert with comments for the Client with respect to the provided data._
* Annex 2 - Fees and billing - only the amount of USD 600,000 is mentioned. Please consider adding payment terms (e.g. 30 days from the date of receipt of the valid VAT invoice etc).

Please let me know how you would like to proceed.

Objective is to determine legal framework around window shopping (price and ETA extractions) for specific country. Here is the methodology we launched : [https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|smart-link] There is also section about legal risk in the methodology. For determining the legal framework the legal council should do following:

* Country legal council  uses [+Legal questionnaire+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-ZjNVX9rtsXA4IWpYt5PR3RVGLfNBY46OdpE7JGvy5g/edit] and checks following: 
** criminal punishment scope for specific country
** civil punishment scope for specific country 
** competitor T&C review
** etc
* Country legal council uses answers to questionnaire to define punishment scope for each window shopping scenario in the [+global risk matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_eWb4mN9Nph8g1OuD0urnNoYmaPGjHEwlKYIMw3KfCU/edit]:
** Punishment scope will be considered every time. But if the  likelihood of the risk materializing is *LOW* than we will not ask about punishment. 

Please let me know if additional questions 🙂

Continuing  Anomaly detection notes, here are project details that I shared during yesterday's meeting (sharing this just to keep track of progress and update other curious ppl who don't attend the meeting):

Even after truncating dimensions of features by creating other category for payment method type and card country, data cardinality is high. For one country and one business line, this is 96 time series  multiplied by number of metrics we want to monitor (so far 4 main metrics). First screenshot with historical validation shows that the model would predict anomalies during >90% of days (combined for all 96 splits payment type-card country). Also, with this approach we can clearly see right away where to look for more details (to understand if something fishy might go on), there are too many potential false positives.
Some caveat was involved there to reduce number of alerts after discussion with Daria:. For monetary metrics, I added another condition: if value of a metrics is less than 500eur, we omit this prediction of anomaly because we don't want to be distracted by these relatively small fluctuations. But it didn't helped much.
I experimented with Principal component analysis to reduce dimensionality of data.
Instead of working with 96 time series, I apply PCA and select its 3 main components. For these 3 time series, I apply the same model as before (Forecasting with Prophet for daily aggregations) and with the same logic, I predict if there are anomalies (an anomaly is identified when the true value of a metrics exceed 99% confidence interval of model prediction).
Another aspect I experimented with: instead of focusing on one metric at a time, I combined all of them at one. For now all meant 2: initial failed payment and gmv. So 96*2 series were reduced to 3 principal components. TODO here: add other metrics as well.
This approach considerably reduced the number of potential alerts. During past year, there would be 20% of days with some sort of anomalies. I look at exact days: it captures LY fraud attack (alerts starting from May 14, 2022) and Applepay preauth AB issues (alerts starting from August 20, 2022).

Next steps:
Add other metrics for PCA modelling (we have # of orders and failed payment counts on a list).
Work on solving interpretability issue with PCA: anomaly in principal component can't tell much exactly what's wrong and doesn't give actionable insight.
One way is to build a second layer prediction: is PCA predicts an anomaly, we run AD model on row data (the model I used before - for each separate payment method and card country split).
Another way involves looking more in PCA itself and trying to map back separate principal components to row data.

* usually contractual penalty is a fixed amount agreed upfront  by the parties., but I see that we currently have some penalties calculated as X/Minute and this has been greenlighted by the external counsel. 

So the method of calculation should be ok from a legal standpoint as long the *penalty applied corresponds to the losses actually incurred by Bolt.* We cannot apply a markup and get money out of a penalty. It should be a simple indemnification of the costs incurred. 

In order to improve the transparency and “sécurité juridique” with the user can we insert a *maximum amount of the penalty? Eg 2.5 E/Liter and in any case not beyond XX EUR.* 

* Same reasoning applies to the administrative fees-> *Administrative Fee* should be equivalent to the costs actually incurred by Bolt for the processing of the Incident/the contractual penalty. 0;5Eur sounds reasonable but would you be able to prove it? 
* Re the *Suspension of 7 days* after the payment is made:  under French law, such a clause may be considered unfair. Indeed, suspension / termination must be limited to cases where the User does not respect his/her essential obligations under the Agreement and in any case to serious reasons. If the user already “paid” by way of the contractual penalty for the breach of T&Cs, adding the suspension afterwards *sounds unfair and may lead to heavy sanctions (7500 EUR in case of illegitimate suspension* and if discriminatory +*criminal sanctions apply : up to 3 years imprisonment + 450K EUR*+) . It is called [refus de vente|https://www.economie.gouv.fr/dgccrf/Publications/Vie-pratique/Fiches-pratiques/refus-de-vente] in FR.

Therefore language referring to driver penalisation or messages sent directly to drivers, particularly with what could be perceived as behaviour instructions are situations leading to a risk of requalification that are recommended to be avoided.

Hi everyone. Let me share with you how we approached this matter in Malta:

# *The issue/situation:* A few months after taking over MT, I realised that there were significant discrepancies of the cooperation quality between our 65 Fleet Partners. In more detail, there were partners known to be non-compliant with local regulations, partners non-responsive, partners with high debt, partners who even tried to lobby myself. This created friction in operations and enhanced risks.

  *2. The task:* The aforementioned situation required some actions in the form of harmonising our cooperation and rewarding partners which were more professional than others.  Seeing the market war between fleets, I had to perform actions that were transparent, clear and equal to everyone.*3. The actions:*

* One of the issues we had internally was that despite being adequently supplied, we were facing partial undersupply for some hours on Saturday evenings. For this reason and tending to solve the aforementioned issue, we implemented a rule for the partners that in order to allow further Couriers onboardings per week, 90% of their Weekly Total Supply Units (Couriers) needs to be online on Saturdays between 18-21.

* Furthermore, in order to control pending debt, we implemented a second rule for partners that in order to allow further Couriers onboardings per week, their *Pending Debt per Weekly Active Courier must be lower than 10 EUR.*

*Pending Debt* = accumulated debt from *Closed Courier Accounts*
*Weekly Active Couriers* = Number of Couriers who have delivered at least one order.*4. The results:*

# *Internal Operational Efficiency has been significantly improved*. We have been able to reduce the working hours of one of the team member (it was her wish to do so) by half without creating any friction.
# *Poor Performing Fleets have faded out*, as they never managed to meet the aforementioned criteria. We are now working with professional partners mitigating in this manner spill over effects in the form of compliance risks etc.
# *Operational Quality metrics have significantly improved*. Undersupply on Saturdays has been improved while our late deliveries > 10min have been reduced by *30% over time.*
# *We managed to decrease our Debt by 24% s*ince the recent implementation of the debt rule, with a decreasing trend.

Hey, Andromeda!

Firstly, I would like to thank you for your patience while waiting for my response regarding this topic and I appreciate your effort in rewriting this article by yourself. 

I reviewed the FAQ article that tackles _Work profiles_ ([How to get a receipt for my work|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360017382159-How-to-get-a-receipt-for-my-work]) and the version you sent to us that you would like us to publish so here are my thoughts: 

* *Introduction*: Did you know that it is possible to receive automatic invoices for trips made using the Fiscal Profile? Each time you pay with the Fiscal Profile, a pre-filled digital invoice will be sent to an email address of your choice. It only takes a few steps to create and use a Tax Profile for free.
** article covers everything you wrote here - it is stated that it is possible to create a Work profile if riders want to receive invoiced with VAT number; it is stated that invoice will be sent to their email address after the trip
* *How do I create a Tax Profile?*: article covers this too:
** *To create a work profile*:
*** Go to the _Work rides_ tab 
*** Fill in the required information. 
** You can also set up your work profile by going to the _Payments_ tab and selecting _Set up your Tax Profile_. )
* *Traveling with a Tax Profile*
Select the Tax Profile as your payment method BEFORE any trip, so that an invoice with tax details is automatically sent to an email address of your choice at the end. That is, fast, easy, and hassle-free — as it should be!
** this part is covered here: *To apply the VAT information to the receipt*, choose the _Fiscal_ profile before ordering a ride. You can do this in the _Payments_ tab of the menu. There you will find the option to choose between your _Personal_ and _Fiscal_ profiles.
* *Access your invoices with tax data*
You will receive the invoice for the trip in your email, where you can download it using the option Download invoice in PDF. If you cannot find the email in your Inbox or Spam, you can request that the invoice be sent again. To do this, go to My trips, select the trip you want, and tap Resend Invoice.
NB: Please be aware that it can take up to 24 hours after a trip for the TIN to be added to a work invoice.
Finally, changing invoice data is a manual process and can take some time. Therefore, it is important that you have a Fiscal Profile created and that it is selected before each trip.
** this is also explained in the article and the article covers most of the notes and instructions you pointed out here 

How-to instructions of a specific feature are generally avoided in our self-help space and from our perspective, this article covers all the relevant information that riders need to create a work profile as well as information on how to get download invoice and that it is necessary to select this payment method *before* requesting a trip, otherwise, they won’t be able to get this a receipt with VAT information. 

I hope I managed to clarify everything to you!

Paula

“““

Regarding your questions about Brand Lift. The assignment to control and test groups is cookie based. Each user is assigned to a group for 14 days, so if a user is in the control group, they will not see the campaign ads for 14 days, but could be exposed to ads later. This is to minimize the impact on the overall campaign reach. In total, the control group size will never be higher than 30% for a Brand Lift study. Technically you could run Conversion Lift study together with a Brand Lift, however, in this case the overall reach of the campaign would be affected more, since the holdback group of 30% is a hard requirement for the whole test period for Conversion Lift studies.

“““



So basically, Brand Lift Studies have the user assigned to a group for 14 days only (and then he sees the ads).



For conversion lift study, we will have to keep the user in the group for the whole period (basically minimizing the reach)

The alert was caused by reaching conntrack limits due to UDP nature.

SG in AWS use conntrack under the hood.

In the case of UDP traffic, the entry in conntrack table lives for 30 sec by default in Linux.

Highly likely AWS implementation of SG has almost the same behavior.

The number of entries in the conntrack table depends on the rate of UDP datagrams from unique clients. This could have no correlation with the raw data rate

In this case, requests to {{coredns}} caused hitting conntrack limits.

We need to scale up {{coredns}} instances for now and think about possible solutions:

* node local DNS cache
* TCP for DNS

Hi,

In Romania we have Decision no. 1.074/2021 regarding the establishment of the guarantee-return system for non-reusable primary packaging. Starting with the date of entry into operation of this system (30 November 2023), the value of the _guarantee_ will be in the amount of 0.5 lei for all types of packaging. The _guarantee_ represents the amount paid by the consumer or end user at the time of purchasing a packaged product, separated from the product price. Thus, traders will be obliged to clearly indicate the value of the _guarantee_.

This system (_guarantee_) is to be implemented at the end of November. Until then, it's up to operators how they set their prices, my opinion is that any additional cost should be included in the final price. But I will read the legislation, to see if we have this provision explained and will return to Legal.

Sorina

The purpose of the test is to:i) improve acceptance rates in cities with high driver rejection rates. By logging off drivers who have no intention of accepting an order, we will improve value proposition to passengers who will often see nearby drivers, but their order does not get accepted.For example:

* We have drivers in cities who are online for over 100 hours, and accept only one or two trips, despite receiving more than 100 order requests. By simply logging drivers off after x number of rejections we can ensure passengers are matched with drivers who are actively willing to accept trips.
* If a driver is automatically logged off after rejecting x number of trips he/she can always log back on without it impacting their activity score.

ii) Ensure better data integrityBy logging off drivers who have no intention of accepting a trip we can ensure better data integrity, as we will see a more accurate reflection of 'online hours' per city from drivers who are willing to accept trips.

SQL for parking

{noformat}with first_parking_push as (
select user_id, min(created) first_push 
from rental.rental_notification_push_notification
where type ='order_bad_parking'
and created_date>date'2022-01-01'
group by 1)
select 
	count(case when further_rides=0 then user_id else null end) users_with_0_rides_after,
	count(case when further_rides>0 and further_rides_with_bad_parking=0 then user_id else null end) users_with_rides_after_no_bp,
	count(case when further_rides>0 and further_rides_with_bad_parking>0 then user_id else null end) users_with_rides_after_bp
from (
	select p.*, 
	t.city_id,
	count(t.order_id) further_rides,
	count(case when t.model_response ='bad_parking' then t.order_id else null end) further_rides_with_bad_parking
from first_parking_push p
left join ng_rental.rental_order_bad_parking_detection_task t  on p.user_id=t.user_id and t.created >p.first_push 
group by 1,2,3
){noformat}

SELECT 
	name
	,billing_name
	,id
	,reg_code
	,vat_code
	,food_price
  	--,commission
	,commission_fee*-1 as commissionfee 
	,commission_fee_VAT*-1 as commissionfee_VAT
	,commission_fee_with_VAT*-1 as comission_plus_VAT
	,campaign_fee
	,campaign_fee_VAT*-1 as campaign_fee_VAT
	,campaign_fee_with_VAT*-1 as campaign_fee_with_VAT
	,shared_campaign_cost*-1 as shared_campaign_cost
	,shared_campaign_cost_VAT*-1 as shared_campaign_cost_VAT
	,shared_campaign_cost_with_VAT*-1 as shared_campaign_with_vat
	,campaign_compensation_fee
	,campaign_compensation_fee_VAT
	,campaign_compensation_fee_with_VAT
    ,adjustment_sum_with_vat*-1	as adjustment
	,total_debt_local-tablet_sell*-1-other_deduction*-1 as total_debt_gross
	,tablet_sell
	,missing_items
	,delivery_bonus
	,other_deduction
    ,total_debt_local
	,ref_number
FROM (
	SELECT provider_provider.legal_name AS name
		,provider_provider.legal_name AS billing_name
		,provider_provider.id AS id		
		,provider_provider.reg_code AS reg_code
		,provider_provider.vat_id AS vat_code
        --,provider_provider.commission AS commission
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyFood'
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS food_price
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN (invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type NOT LIKE '%payout%'
						AND invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type NOT LIKE '%payment%')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS total_debt_local	
	--- Commission_fee ---			
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyFee'
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount - invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS commission_fee	
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyFee'
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS commission_fee_VAT
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyFee'
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS commission_fee_with_VAT
	--- Campaign_fee ---
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyCampaign_fee'
						THEN abs(invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount - invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6) 
					ELSE 0  
					END), 2) AS campaign_fee		
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyCampaign_fee'
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0  
					END), 2) AS campaign_fee_VAT
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type = 'providerCompanyCampaign_fee'
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount
					ELSE 0  
					END), 2) AS campaign_fee_with_VAT					
	--- Shared campaign cost ---
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type in ('providerCompanySharedCampaignCostDelivery','providerCompanySharedCampaignCostFood')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount - invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS shared_campaign_cost		
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type in ('providerCompanySharedCampaignCostDelivery','providerCompanySharedCampaignCostFood')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS shared_campaign_cost_VAT			
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type in ('providerCompanySharedCampaignCostDelivery','providerCompanySharedCampaignCostFood')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS shared_campaign_cost_with_VAT	
	--- Campaign compensation fee ---			
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type in ('providerCompanyCampaign_compensation')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount - invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS campaign_compensation_fee
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type in ('providerCompanyCampaign_compensation')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount/6
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS campaign_compensation_fee_VAT	
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.external_type in ('providerCompanyCampaign_compensation')
						THEN invoicing_balance_balance_entry.amount
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS campaign_compensation_fee_with_VAT
	FROM glue.ng_payout.invoicing_balance_balance_entry AS invoicing_balance_balance_entry
	LEFT JOIN glue.ng_payout.invoicing_balance_account AS invoicing_balance_account ON invoicing_balance_account.id = invoicing_balance_balance_entry.account_id
	LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates AS currency_exchange_rates ON invoicing_balance_balance_entry.currency = currency_exchange_rates.currency
		AND (DATE (invoicing_balance_balance_entry.created)) = (DATE (currency_exchange_rates.valid_on))
	LEFT JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_provider_provider_company AS provider_provider ON invoicing_balance_account.external_id = provider_provider.id
		AND invoicing_balance_account.type like '%food_restaurant_company%'
	LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city AS admin_system_city ON provider_provider.city_id = admin_system_city.id
	LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_country AS admin_system_country ON admin_system_city.country_code = admin_system_country.code
	WHERE invoicing_balance_balance_entry.created_date > date '2023-04-15'
		and invoicing_balance_balance_entry.created_date < date '2023-05-15'
        and invoicing_balance_balance_entry.created >= timestamp '2023-04-24' - interval '2' hour
		and invoicing_balance_balance_entry.created < timestamp '2023-05-01'  - interval '2' hour 
		and invoicing_balance_account.type = 'food_restaurant_company'
		AND (admin_system_country.code = 'ua')
	GROUP BY 1
		,2
		,3
		,4
		,5
	)
LEFT JOIN (
	SELECT 	i.to_agent_id AS id
		,substring(i.public_id, 1, position('-' in i.public_id)-1) ref_number
        ,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN iir.title ='adjustment_type_refund'
						THEN iir.sum_with_vat
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS adjustment_sum_with_vat
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN iir.title in ('adjustment_type_tablet_sell','adjustment_type_tablet_rent')
						THEN iir.sum_with_vat
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS tablet_sell			
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN iir.title = 'adjustment_type_deduction'
						THEN iir.sum_with_vat
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS other_deduction
	---New Columns!!!----
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN iir.title = 'adjustment_type_missing_items'
						THEN iir.sum_with_vat
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS missing_items
		,COALESCE(SUM(CASE 
					WHEN iir.title = 'adjustment_type_delivery_bonus'
						THEN iir.sum_with_vat
					ELSE 0
					END), 2) AS delivery_bonus						
	FROM glue.ng_payout.invoicing_document_invoice_row iir
    LEFT JOIN (select id, invoice_date_local, to_agent_id, public_id, city_id, period_end from glue.ng_payout.invoicing_document_invoice where public_id is not null 
	and created_date > date '2023-04-15' and created_date < date '2023-05-15') i ON iir.invoice_id = i.id
	LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city city ON i.city_id = city.id
	WHERE i.period_end >= date '2023-04-24'
		AND i.period_end < date '2023-05-01'
		AND city.country_code = 'ua'
		and iir.type = 'provider_company_fee' 
	GROUP BY 1
    , 2
	) using (id)
	where 
  total_debt_local!=0
  and reg_code = '23744453'{noformat}

Additionally, I’m  attaching Special Terms with reflected change in Schedule 2, clause 7.1.



*1. As far as I know Marinopoulos will not have any type of storage regarding GDPR data (maybe except a very small amount in a type of ‘‘cache’’ memory).*

Yes, the scope of data accessible to Partners is limited. Data sharing terms relate only to the processing operations that relate to personal data and naturally are not relevant to anonymous data.

*2. Since Marinopoulos is not transmitting any data to any third party at all it may not be considered as a data controller.*

Please note that according to Bolt Food Platform Terms and Conditions, the underlying sale agreement is concluded by and between Partner and the end-user and in that capacity we believe that the Partner would act as a data controller. Personal data from Bolt Food Platform is functionally used by both parties for their own separate purposes (by Bolt to provide information society service, by the Partner to conclude sale agreement with the end-user) and both parties are making either general or specific decision on how the data is processed. 

*3. Marinopoulos has not received any type of consent from the initial data owners (Bolt customers) in order to receive GDPR data thus may not be a data controller.*

The consent is not the only legal basis that would legitimise processing personal data. One of the legal basis that is expressed in article 6 of the GDPR is the contractual necessity - i.e. the processing is lawful if it is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract. Given that the sale agreement would be concluded by the Partner, this would be aligned with the premise set out in article 6(1)(b) of the GDPR.

*4. According to the above-mentioned points Marinopoulos is not directly able nor responsible to fulfill any type of request regarding the rights that potentially the GDPR subjects may need to exercise.*

We are in the position that Marinopoulos will have to deliver on the data subject requests, but only in the very limited capacity where it acts as a data controller. The majority of clients' data collected via Bolt Food app is not available to Partners and in regards to such data, Bolt would be considered a sole data controller and is responsible for executing data subject requests.

Hi [~accountid:6320602ec7601c8e4abeda47] here is a short summary and attached is the full legal memo if you wish to consider this in more detail. Unsurprisingly, the external counsel view is very cautious. Please see below.

[^20230502 Bolt - Legal opinion on data scraping.pdf]

+Civil Liability+

A Bolt employee who agrees to the competitors’ T&Cs in question would be personally liable for any breach of the T&Cs – but not to the exclusion of Bolt as mandator and beneficiary. Bolt would also be exposed to an ancillary action in tort as the employer, mandator and beneficiary of the data/information scraped by its employee - if a claim for payment of damages was brought by Uber/Ecabs. In the opinion of the external counsel, Bolt would not be entirely shielded from civil responsibility by engaging a third party (not an employee) to scrape the data, either, even if the third party is a mercenary seller of the data scraped, and this because, liability under Maltese tort law is based on the concept of fault.

However it is impossible to advise on the quantum of damages which either Bolt or the employee would be exposed to - as this would depend on the damage actually suffered (and any future loss of earnings) by the competitors. This does play to our advantage since the competitor would need to establish a causal link between the actions of Bolt and the damages. 

+Criminal Liability+

Taking a conservative approach, the external counsel opines that an employee carrying out the data scarping may be held criminally liable under Article 337C(1)(c) and (j) of the Criminal Code, for making use of data in a way other than the intended purpose - which purposes, one can argue, is provided under the T&Cs of each of the competitors. Criminal liability could also extend to Bolt for making use of the data gathered through an employee’s actions, and this in terms of Article 337C (1)(f) of the Criminal Code which refers to taking possession of or make use of any data (even data obtained by others). 

The punishment for contravening the provisions of Article 337 is a fine not exceeding €23,293.73 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 4 years, or to both such fine and imprisonment. If the offence caused serious damages, the penalty would be increased to a fine (multa) of not less than €500 and not exceeding €150,000 or to imprisonment for a term from 12 months to 10 years, or to both such fine and imprisonment.

Please let me know if you have any questions? 

Thanks, 

Liisa

Indeed, what the Country Manager mentioned, according to _Decision no. 947/2000 on the method of indicating the prices of products offered to consumers for sale_ says that:

_"selling price = the final price for a given unit or quantity of the product, including value added tax and all additional taxes;"_

Additional taxes generally refer to the taxes you have to pay for certain products (like special taxes).

But, I read the entire Decision and I identified in Art. 3, paragraph (3) the following: "_Delivery service charges -_ *_packaging and transport - may be mentioned separately_*_, provided they are clear, easily identifiable and legible."_

_(4) The seller is responsible for indicating the selling price and the price per unit of measure."_

Therefore, these costs can be mentioned separately, right Magda? I understand that the problem here was whether we are against any law if we provide the costs separately.

Hi all,
I had a call with NS (national train company) today, who do their integrations via Rivier. In summary:

* NS has changed their approach to external integrations. They used to be reluctant, now they really want to push this in the coming 2 years, including through media campaigns to users. The first focus ons on bikes/scooters/carsharing, but also taxis are interesting and they are not happy with their current taxi partner, as they are not flexible enough.
* NS has a significant preference to do the integration through Rivier. If that's not at all possible, a direct integration with NS could be envisaged, but it would be an exceptional procedure and require a lot of internal coordination on their side, which would take time. So they strongly suggest to go via Rivier.
* On the shared mobility side, they already have OV fiets, Donkey and MyWheels, and will start full integration with TIER in June.
* NS cannot impose fines on users; any payments other than the price of the ride need to be handled by the MSP directly
* commercial terms: NS asks for a commission of 10%, for both taxi and shared mobility
* Timeline for NS: anything between Q4/2023 and Q2/2024 is realistic

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] ,  

I added [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] as a participant in the ticket and once she is back I will be able to provide you with more detailed feedback. On Monday, I have a discussion planned with Andrea Vota to clarify the concerned regulatory constraints as you have suggested.

Below are my initial thoughts on the two questions raised:

* +whether renting electric cars to drivers directly would increase our reclassification risk+

On a first and high level review, it would appear that renting cars to the drivers directly would seem to increase our reclassification risk since one of the legal presumption criteria of employment could arguably be met through this activity.

A new amendment of the Labour Code entered into force on May 1st 2023, establishing a presumption of employment in relation to digital platforms. The new article 12-A establishes that “ _an employment contract is presumed to exist when, in the relationship between the activity provider and the digital platform some of the following characteristics are verified: ... f) the equipment and work instruments/tools used belong to the digital platform or are operated by them through a lease agreement/rental contract._”

Our outside counsel is of the view that this means that the instruments/tools are made available by the platform to the worker, regardless of whether the platform owns them or uses them under a rental contract. The criterion will not be met if, for instance, none of the tools used by the courier were provided by the platform. 

Additionally, renting tools to the couriers could lead to one arguing that Bolt intends to decide and control what tools are used, and instead of providing them for free, demands that couriers buy/rent them in order to prevent the criterion from applying.

*  +whether there are any regulatory restrictions to do that+

I will have a discussion with Andrea Vota next week on this topic and then be able to provide you some feedback. Nevertheless, I would like to point out that in PT law No. 45/2018 of August 10th establishes the so-called “legal regime of the activity of individual and remunerated and remunerated transport of passengers in vehicles from an electronic platform”, in short, TVDE law.

On a quick review, the TVDE  law establishes that:

# electronic platforms “_may not … finance or be a party to an interested party in business relating to the acquisition, renting, leasing or leasing or other form of use of TVDE vehicles._” 
# “It is forbidden to place or display advertising inside or outside the vehicle performing TVDE.”

Thank you!

Mostly can be completed. Medium size project (1-2 weeks). More details for reference:

* *Storing ‘permanent error’ and ‘fraud error’ in DB*
** Statistics aggregation using error message in real-time would be a performance bottleneck, thus the type of error has to be determined already during data being saved into {{user_payment_adding_attempt}} table (e.g. new ENUM column)
** Mapping of errors messages to error type can be initially be hardcoded in server logic
*** E.g. {{PAYMENT_ERROR_FRAUD}} and {{card.possible-fraud}} are mapped to {{error_fraud}}
*** Initial scope would not include UI configuration capabilities
** Code [reference|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4665d8d3aa46e5ca30f9ccf7b77480e2d2a0c6bc/src/platform/commerce/fraud_data/main/sync/cron/UserPaymentAddingAttemptCron.ts#L82]
* *total count of card adding errors user has:*
** Possible as we are already doing it now for ‘4 weeks count’
** Additional queries/logic needs to be added for month/week/day stats
** Loader code [reference|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/a63548aa56e900be96a2478d61d6b79dccb7ab38/src/platform/commerce/fraud/main/order/service/OrderCheckDataGatheringService.ts#L72]
** Data aggregator code [reference|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/ffefaf4abf481ff802b88fc17c3377c425924173/src/platform/commerce/fraud_data/main/payment_data/service/UserDataService.ts#L266]
* *count of permanent errors user has*
** Additional logic to count stats based on the new ENUM column (see first point in the list)
* *count of fraud/suspicion errors user has:*
** Additional logic to count stats based on the new ENUM column (see first point in the list)
* *count of distinct card countries the user tried to add*
** Out of scope - we already provide list of distinct card countries
* *count of distinct card countries the user tried to add where Bolt doesn’t have operations*
** Out of scope as we don’t have a proper list of ‘active’ countries to rely on
** Agreed with Guilherme that the list of non-active countries will be checked in fraud rules using list of distinct card counries
** Future potential solution is to use system countries: [https://admin.prelive.bolt.eu/admin/SystemCountry/|https://admin.prelive.bolt.eu/admin/SystemCountry/]
